evidence_set: Coronary heart disease, carriers of the intake-lowering ADH1B variant against non-carriers: odds ratio 0.90 (95% CI 0.84 to 0.96; I² 17%; 46 studies, 20,259 events in 168,731 people); in the four studies with at least 1,000 events (8,374 events), 0.81 (0.72 to 0.91). In the Methods the authors stated that, if the observational U shape were causal, carriers should have higher coronary risk among people drinking more than 0 to under 21 UK units a week and lower risk among people drinking 21 or more.

evidence_set: 161,498 adults genotyped for ALDH2 rs671 and ADH1B rs1229984 (151,028 chosen at random). In men, rs671 AA, AG and GG went with mean intakes of 3, 37 and 157 g a week and rs1229984 AA, AG and GG with 98, 106 and 157 g a week; the six genotype–area groups had mean male intakes of 4, 18, 34, 78, 130 and 256 g a week, with 3% to 74% of men ever drinking in most weeks; in women, mean intake was below 2 g a week in groups 1 to 3 and 4 to 8 g a week in groups 4 to 6.

UK Biobank, 371,463 people of European genetic ancestry; primary score of 5 variants associated with alcohol use disorder, strongly associated with intake (F statistic 780). Linear Mendelian randomization, odds ratio per 1-SD increase in genetically predicted consumption (an SD not defined in the main text): coronary artery disease 1.38 (95% CI 1.10 to 1.74; P = 6.00×10−3); myocardial infarction 1.37 (1.05 to 1.78; P = 2.00×10−2), above the paper's threshold of P < .008 for six diseases. Weighted median, MR-Egger, MR-PRESSO and analyses excluding abstainers pointed the same way.

Methods › Study Population; Methods › Genetic Instruments for Alcohol Consumption; Results › Associations Between Genetic Instruments and Alcohol Intake Phenotypes; Results › Traditional MR, 2nd paragraph; Table 2

Nonlinear Mendelian randomization with the primary score: quadratic models fitted best for coronary artery disease and hypertension (P < .001), with every amount of intake associated with higher risk, rising more steeply at higher intake; the fitted curves print no values. With the secondary score (10 variants for the AUDIT-C consumption score), piecewise analyses suggested no rise in cardiovascular risk until roughly 7 to 14 drinks a week, with slight decreases at modest intake for hypertension and in some analyses in women, which the authors attribute to pleiotropy in that score and low power.
Methods › Genetic Instruments for Alcohol Consumption; Results › Evaluating Association Shapes, 1st to 3rd paragraphs; Figures 2 and 3

In 34,423 lifelong abstainers the score showed no association with the continuous traits reported in that paragraph (the main text gives no disease results for abstainers), except HDL cholesterol and apolipoprotein A, which the authors call a potential pleiotropic effect; MR-Egger intercepts were non-significant. The authors acknowledge that the associations may reflect genes that influence both drinking and cardiovascular disease rather than an effect of alcohol, and that variants for diagnosed alcohol use disorder are an indirect proxy for usual intake.

evidence_set: 512,715 adults from ten areas of China, enrolled 2004–2008 and followed about 10 years to 1 January 2017 (0.9% lost to follow-up); 161,498 genotyped for ALDH2 rs671 and ADH1B rs1229984.
